task1.title: Number of tourists visiting a Caribbean island (2010–2017)
task1.prompt: The graph below shows the number of tourists visiting a particular Caribbean island between 2010 and 2017.

chartDesc.title: Number of tourists visiting a Caribbean island (2010–2017)
chartDesc.overview: Overall, total tourist numbers grew continuously over the 7-year period, rising from 1.0 million to 3.5 million. Although staying on the island was initially the more popular option, cruise ship visitors grew at a much faster rate and surpassed island visitors in 2016.
keyFeatures: Total visitor numbers increased steadily from 1.0 million in 2010 to a peak of 3.5 million in 2017.
Visitors staying on cruise ships surged from 0.25 million in 2010 to 2.0 million in 2017.
Visitors staying on the island doubled from 0.75 million in 2010 to 1.5 million in 2013, remaining unchanged until a brief drop in 2016 (1.25 million) before recovering to 1.5 million in 2017.
In 2016, cruise ship visitors (1.5 million) overtook visitors staying on the island (1.25 million) for the first time.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Printed newspapers and books versus reading online
task2.prompt:
In the future, nobody will buy printed newspapers or books because they will be able to read everything they want online without paying.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
